Dan: hey team, first day on runtime. trying to build from source on ubuntu 24.04 with cuda 11.8 and gcc 12. hitting a ptxas error at link, any quick tips?
Dan: paste of error:
````
ptxas fatal : ValueError: unsupported PTX version '8.7'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
````
Dan: my build command: `make -j8 BUILD_USE_CUDA=1` on main
Mika: welcome! short checks: `nvcc --version`, `nvidia-smi`, and ensure CUDA_HOME -> /usr/local/cuda-11.8. also driver should be >=525.x for 11.8 ideally
Dan: nvcc: Cuda compilation tools, release 11.8, V11.8.89 ; nvidia-smi shows Driver Version: 520.61.05
Natanael: that driver is probably the root cause. ptxas unsupported PTX often means toolkit produced PTX the driver can't handle. if you can't upgrade driver, try building for a lower arch or set TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST to avoid generating PTX v8.7
Evan: also check `ptxas --version` and `which ptxas` in case an older/newer ptxas from /usr/local/cuda vs packaged distro is used. gcc mismatch gives different errors, but worth checking `CUDAHOSTCXX` too
Dan: `which ptxas` -> /usr/local/cuda-11.8/bin/ptxas ; `ptxas --version` -> 10.6.0
Rosie: if driver upgrade isn't an option (corp laptop), you can pass `-gencode arch=compute_70,code=sm_70` or set TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="7.0;7.5" to limit generated PTX. also grep build logs for `-gencode` lines
Dan: tried TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=sm_70, build moved past ptxas but now hits `undefined reference to cublasLtCreate` during link
Evan: that one is link order / missing lib. ensure `-lcublasLt` is linked (and before -lcublas/-lcudart). check /usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64/libcublasLt.so exists
Dan: libcublasLt.so is present; changing link order to `-lcublasLt -lcublas -lcudart` fixed the linker. build now completed! :tada:
Dan: i'll add an onboarding note: driver min version, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST workaround, and cublasLt link-order gotcha. will share gist of commands I ran
Mika: please ping me and i'll add to eng-runtime onboarding doc. welcome aboard! :wave:
infra-bot: CI image for runtime builds: registry.redwood/internal/runtime-dev:cuda11.8-gcc12-2026-02-15
Rosie: if you need a reproducible env, infra's runtime-dev docker image is easiest; opens GPU passthrough caveats for corp laptops though.
Dan: thanks everyone — saved my morning. will follow up with doc and gist
